title: One module records the household as a tenant and the other records it as owning and occupying the home.
detail: These cannot both be true of the same residence, and the two readings point at opposite policies rather than at different limits on one. A tenant's policy answers personal property, loss of use, personal liability and medical payments, and the landlord does not provide insurance for the tenant's personal property [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. An owner-occupier's policy is built around a dwelling limit, which should be the amount it would cost to replace the home and may have nothing to do with its purchase price or market value [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. The loss of use limit is measured differently in each: normally 20 percent of Coverage A on a homeowners policy, and 20 percent of Coverage C on a renters policy [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. Every earthquake finding that assumes a companion residential policy of one kind is unsafe while this disagreement stands, because the wrong companion form changes what the earthquake cover sits on top of.
action: Establish who owns the residence and correct whichever module is wrong before relying on either module's findings. If one module was completed for a different property, complete it again for this one rather than editing it into place.
author: Aaron Bollinger
